sections.h2: Choices for selling an Irving house
sections.html:
In Irving you can hire an agent, find your own buyer or accept a cash offer for the house as it stands. Which one wins depends on condition, debt and the date you need to be done.

Irving sits in western Dallas County along State Highways 183 and 114, about 12 miles west of downtown Dallas, between the Elm and West Forks of the Trinity River. The city reports 264,546 residents and a daytime population above 300,000, so many employees look for housing near work. With plenty of competing listings, price and condition decide how long yours sits.

  • Agent: best for a house in good order.
  • Own buyer: no listing fee, more forms to handle.
  • Cash: no repairs, no showings.

sections.h2: Irving neighborhoods and who buys in them
sections.html:
Irving began as a rail town. The Chicago, Rock Island and Gulf Railway founders held a lot auction on December 19, 1903, and voters incorporated the city in 1914. Farmland turned into subdivisions fast: 2,615 people in 1950, 45,895 in 1960 and 100,996 by 1970.

Today you find mid-century neighborhoods, newer Las Colinas areas and a large share of rental property, and each draws a different buyer. The economy leans corporate, with about 8,500 businesses and Dallas-Fort Worth Airport along the western edge. Many buyers are relocating employees working to a deadline. A firm closing date, clear title and move-in condition give you an edge with them.

Irving's property tax goes to the Dallas County Tax Office. Visit the Records Building downtown at 500 Elm Street, Suite 3300, call customer care at 214-653-7811, or pay online.

Use the county site for figures on your own parcel, and ask for a payoff statement well before closing.

sections.h2: Permits and open work on an Irving house
sections.html: Permits run through city staff. After a remodel or a new deck, check that the permit was actually closed out. A permit left open is a classic reason for a closing to slip, and clearing it before you list is cheaper than scrambling mid-contract.

The Dallas County clerk records Irving deeds. The state's published schedule looks like this.

First page$5.00

Fees change, so ask the clerk for the total on your own instrument. The title company usually files for you.

More Irving residents rent than own, so a seller may well be holding a house with a tenant in it. The first step is a written notice to vacate. Unless the lease says otherwise it gives a few days, and it can be handed over, mailed or e-mailed if the lease allows.

  • If the tenant stays, the landlord sues in justice court and the tenant is served before trial.
  • A hearing follows within a few weeks.
  • Anyone appealing to county court has a very short deadline after judgment.
  • After a final judgment comes a writ of possession, with warning before removal.

Certain covered properties carry a longer federal notice. Before you promise any buyer an empty house, speak with an attorney.

sections.h2: Using a cash sale to clear tax or lien trouble
sections.html:
Selling for cash helps with tax or lien trouble as long as the proceeds cover what is owed at the table. The tax lien is created in January and stays with the property, which is why the closing agent will demand that unpaid taxes be settled. Whoever owned the house that January also remains liable for that year's levy after the sale.

From February 1 penalty and interest run, an attorney's collection surcharge can be added, and some collectors allow installments on a homestead. Before you accept any offer, get a payoff figure from the Dallas County Tax Office and have the closing agent check every lien.

sections.h2: What if an Irving owner dies without a will?
sections.html:
Before an heir can sell, authority has to be shown. If there is a will, it is generally offered for probate within four years of the death. Without one, a modest estate may use a small estate affidavit when every heir agrees, though a court must approve it.

A transfer on death deed, if recorded before the owner passed, moves the house outside probate. An affidavit of heirship is another route, although a buyer is free to refuse it. A Dallas County probate lawyer can say which one fits, ideally before the house goes on the market.

Adverse possession is open and visible use of land under a claim hostile to the owner. Section 16.026 of the Civil Practice and Remedies Code sets a ten-year period, and a claimant sues as a trespass to try title case.

The realistic risk at an unattended Irving house is a squatter rather than a title claim. Under Property Code chapter 24B an owner may ask the sheriff or constable for removal, within limits. Keeping a vacant house secured, visited and insured is the better protection, and a quick sale can end the exposure.

sections.h2: Getting an Irving house ready for a fast close
sections.html: Relocation buyers value certainty. A tidy file, meaning the deed, a payoff letter and a current Dallas County tax statement, does more for you than a few extra dollars of staging. Settle early whether you will repair, sell as-is or price for a renovator, then weigh each written offer by closing date, title charges and the buyer's likely reaction to inspection.

sections.h2: Why corporate buyers shape Irving offers
sections.html:
Many Irving buyers come through an employer, so their timelines are tight and their questions concrete: when can we close, is the title clean, and does the house need work they would have to arrange from another city? Answer all three in the first conversation and you can beat a slightly higher offer.

Landlords see the other side of this. An investor may happily keep the tenant in a leased rental, but an empty house shows better to a family that plans to live in it. Pick your target buyer before setting the price.

The recorded deed and a current Dallas County tax statement come first. With a loan outstanding, ask for the payoff in writing so the closing agent knows the exact balance. Add permit records for any remodel or deck, plus the lease on a rented house, and a payoff for each lien. With those in hand a title company can run its search quickly, and a wary buyer sees that nothing is hidden.

Include a brief note on the roof, the foundation and the main systems. A cash buyer can price faster from honest notes, and they protect you if a dispute surfaces after closing.

sections.h2: The step-by-step sale from listing to keys
sections.html: The sale runs in four stages. First you set a price and pick a route. Next you accept an offer and open title. Third comes inspection, where a loan buyer may ask for repairs and a cash buyer usually will not. Last is closing, where you sign before a notary and the Dallas County clerk files the deed. Between the final two stages the closing agent confirms taxes and liens, so surprises come out before you sign.

faqs.a: Dallas County, in its western part, along State Highways 183 and 114.

faqs.q: Where do I pay Irving property taxes?
faqs.a: The Dallas County Tax Office, online or at its downtown Records Building at 500 Elm Street, Suite 3300.

faqs.q: What does the Dallas County clerk charge?
faqs.a: A set fee per page plus a handful of smaller records fees. For an exact total, ask the clerk.

faqs.q: How long is a Texas tenant's notice to vacate?
faqs.a: Written notice, normally a few days unless the lease differs. Covered properties may fall under a longer federal notice.

faqs.q: Does unpaid tax follow the house to a buyer?
faqs.a: The lien stays with the property, so closing agents ask for payment at or before closing.
